name: Trilobite
fact: Trilobites swam, crawled and burrowed in the seas for about 270 million years.

name: Brachiopod
fact: Brachiopods look like clams but belong to an entirely different animal group.

name: Crinoid Stem
fact: Crinoids are animals, nicknamed sea lilies, and their stem discs are very common fossils.

name: Horn Coral
fact: Horn corals were solitary corals shaped like a curved horn, common in Paleozoic seas.

name: Bryozoan Colony
fact: Bryozoans are tiny colonial animals whose fossils often look like delicate lace.

name: Graptolite
fact: Graptolite fossils look like pencil marks on shale; the name means 'written in stone'.

name: Sea Snail
fact: Gastropods, the snail group, have left shells in rocks for over 500 million years.

name: Clam Shell
fact: Bivalve shells are among the most common marine fossils found anywhere.

name: Fish Scale
fact: Many Devonian fishes wore thick, bony scales as armor.

name: Urchin Spine
fact: Sea urchin spines fall off after death, so they turn up often as fossils.

name: Petrified Wood
fact: Petrified wood forms when minerals slowly replace wood, preserving its grain.

name: Fern Frond
fact: Coal-age swamps were full of giant club mosses, horsetails and tree ferns.

name: Scale Tree Bark
fact: Lepidodendron, the scale tree, was a giant relative of modern club mosses.

name: Coprolite
fact: Coprolites are fossilized dung that reveal what ancient animals ate.

name: Ammonite
fact: Ammonites were shelled cephalopods, distant cousins of squid and octopus.

name: Orthocone
fact: Orthocones were cephalopods with straight shells, and some grew very large.

name: Belemnite Guard
fact: Belemnites were squid-like animals; the bullet-shaped fossil is their internal guard.

name: Enrolled Trilobite
fact: Some trilobites could curl into a ball for defense, like a modern pill bug.

name: Eurypterid
fact: Eurypterids, called sea scorpions, were not true scorpions.

name: Goniatite
fact: Goniatites were early ammonoids with simple zigzag lines on their shells.

name: Ichthyosaur Vertebra
fact: Ichthyosaurs were dolphin-shaped marine reptiles that gave birth to live young.

name: Glossopteris Leaf
fact: Glossopteris leaves are found on several southern continents, supporting continental drift.

name: Dimetrodon Tooth
fact: Dimetrodon had a sail on its back and is closer kin to mammals than to dinosaurs.

name: Crinoid Crown
fact: A crinoid with its arms intact is a rare find, since the body falls apart after death.

name: Phytosaur Tooth
fact: Phytosaurs looked like crocodiles but belonged to a separate reptile lineage.

name: Coelophysis Bone
fact: Coelophysis was a small, slender, early dinosaur of the Late Triassic.

name: Meganeura Wing
fact: Meganeura was a giant dragonfly-like insect with a wingspan over half a meter.

name: Dunkleosteus Plate
fact: Dunkleosteus was an armored fish whose jaws bore sharp bony plates instead of teeth.

name: Anomalocaris Appendage
fact: Anomalocaris was a top Cambrian predator, often fossilized as just its grasping limbs.

name: Archaeopteryx Feather
fact: Archaeopteryx had feathers and wings, yet also teeth and a long bony tail.

name: Shark Tooth
fact: Sharks shed teeth constantly, so their fossil teeth are plentiful.

name: Oyster Shell
fact: Oysters have built dense shell beds in the sea since the Triassic.

name: Sand Dollar
fact: Sand dollars are flattened sea urchins that burrow through sandy seabeds.

name: Turritella Snail
fact: Turritella are tall, spiral sea snails that are abundant in many Cenozoic rocks.

name: Scallop Shell
fact: Scallops swim by clapping their two shells together.

name: Reef Coral
fact: Reef corals build limestone reefs that can outlast the animals themselves.

name: Nummulite
fact: Nummulites are coin-shaped shells of giant single-celled organisms.

name: Leaf Impression
fact: Leaf impressions reveal what ancient forests looked like.

name: Gar Scale
fact: Gars are ancient fishes with hard, diamond-shaped scales.

name: Crab Claw
fact: Crab claws are tough, so they fossilize more often than whole crabs.

name: Turtle Shell Piece
fact: Turtle shells are built from fused bone, which helps them survive burial.

name: Crocodile Scute
fact: Crocodile relatives have bony plates called scutes embedded in their skin.

name: Lignite
fact: Lignite is soft brown coal formed from buried plant matter.

name: Conifer Cone
fact: Fossil cones show which conifers grew in ancient forests.

name: Baculite
fact: Baculites were ammonites with straight shells instead of coiled ones.

name: Mosasaur Tooth
fact: Mosasaurs were giant marine reptiles related to monitor lizards.

name: Plesiosaur Tooth
fact: Plesiosaurs were marine reptiles with four paddle-shaped flippers.

name: Fossil Horse Tooth
fact: Horses started out small and had several toes on each foot.

name: Amber Piece
fact: Amber is fossil tree resin and can trap tiny insects for millions of years.

name: Dinosaur Eggshell
fact: Fossil eggshell fragments show where dinosaurs once nested.

name: Sea Cow Rib
fact: The ancestors of manatees once walked on four legs.

name: Pterosaur Bone
fact: Pterosaur bones were thin and hollow, so they rarely survive as fossils.

name: Hadrosaur Tooth
fact: Hadrosaurs ground plants with hundreds of tightly packed teeth.

name: Ankylosaur Armor
fact: Ankylosaurs were covered in bony plates embedded in their skin.

name: Basilosaurus Tooth
fact: Basilosaurus was an early whale that still had tiny hind limbs.

name: Titanoboa Vertebra
fact: Titanoboa was a giant snake that lived after the dinosaurs died out.

name: Smilodon Canine
fact: Smilodon's famous saber teeth were long but relatively fragile.

name: Megalodon Tooth
fact: Megalodon teeth can be larger than a human hand.

name: T. rex Tooth
fact: Tyrannosaurus rex had thick, deeply rooted teeth built for crushing bone.

name: Mammoth Tusk
fact: Woolly mammoth tusks kept growing throughout the animal's life.
